# Final Review Proposals

You are a code reviewer. Review the changes in this project for correctness, safety, and robustness.

Run `git diff` to see all changes, then read the key implementation files end-to-end. For each issue found, cite specific files and line numbers.

Ignore style and cosmetics — only report real bugs, safety problems, correctness gaps, and significant maintainability risks.

## Project Prompt

○ tanksim-6e5.4.5 · Upgrade source-water profiles to carry carbonate-relevant inputs and differentiated defaults   [● P1 · OPEN]
Owner: master · Type: task
Created: 2026-03-26 · Updated: 2026-03-27
Labels: carbonates, data, phase-2, scientific-core, source-water

Context:
- The shipped source-water presets currently differ in GH/KH/TDS-like dimensions, but not enough in pH behavior to justify their names.
- The new carbonate model needs source-water data that actually drives differentiated equilibrium outcomes.

Deliverable:
- Extend source-water presets so they include whatever carbonate-relevant inputs the chosen model requires (e.g., equilibrium pH or pCO2 target).
- Revisit the shipped presets (hard_shrimp, moderate, soft_acidic, ro_like) so their behavior is meaningfully differentiated.
- Update any docs/comments explaining what each profile is trying to emulate.

Expected differentiation after upgrade:
  hard_shrimp: KH 8, high DIC → pH 7.5-8.0, well-buffered
  moderate: KH 4, moderate DIC → pH 7.0-7.5
  soft_acidic: KH 2-3, low DIC → pH 6.5-7.0, weakly buffered
  ro_like: KH 0.1, minimal DIC → pH 5.5-6.5, very poorly buffered

Likely touch points:
- crates/tank_core/src/types/source_water.rs
- crates/tank_data/data/source_water/*.toml
- crates/tank_data/src/presets.rs

## Acceptance Criteria

Acceptance Criteria:
- source-water presets no longer collapse into nearly identical pH behavior under the new model
- preset semantics are documented in plain language
- tests can load each preset successfully through the updated data path

Dependencies:
  -> tanksim-6e5.4.2 (blocks) - Implement explicit carbonate equilibrium and pH solver
  -> tanksim-6e5.4 (parent-child) - Phase 2 — carbonate chemistry, CO2 exchange, and pH realism
  -> tanksim-6e5.2.6 (blocks) - Retune process parameters and scenario defaults after normalization

Dependents:
  <- tanksim-6e5.7.2 (blocks) - Attach provenance and confidence metadata to high-value chemistry and ecology parameters
  <- tanksim-6e5.6.5 (blocks) - Model chloride protection against nitrite hazard and integrate toxic stress accounting
  <- tanksim-6e5.6.3 (blocks) - Add mineral budget and molt success/failure mechanics
  <- tanksim-6e5.4.6 (blocks) - Add carbonate regression tests and scenario probes

Comments:
  [2026-03-26 13:46 UTC] backlog-planner: Rationale:
- Source water is one of the most intuitive scientific levers for players, so the presets should teach something real.
- This bead also sets up later shrimp mineral/toxicity work (F3, F5) by making water profiles richer and clearer.
- Avoid overfitting to one real-world tap-water case; target distinct, interpretable envelopes instead.

Real-world reference points:
- Hard shrimp water (Sulawesi-type or high-KH tap): KH 6-10°, GH 6-10°, pH 7.5-8.2
- Moderate community water (typical treated tap): KH 3-6°, GH 4-8°, pH 7.0-7.5
- Soft acidic (blackwater, some Asian tap): KH 0-2°, GH 2-4°, pH 5.5-6.8
- RO/DI remineralized: KH 0-1°, GH 3-5° (added minerals), pH 6.0-7.0
  [2026-03-26 17:08 UTC] reviewer: Unit test requirements:

1. test_source_water_carries_dic: Source water profiles include DIC/CO2 concentration. Verify soft_acidic, moderate, hard_shrimp, ro_like all have reasonable DIC values.
2. test_source_water_carries_alkalinity: All profiles have alkalinity values matching their GH/KH character (soft water: low KH/alkalinity, hard water: high KH/alkalinity).
3. test_water_change_brings_source_dic: After water change with hard_shrimp source, water DIC shifts toward source DIC proportional to change percentage.
4. test_water_change_brings_source_alkalinity: Same for alkalinity — verify dilution math is correct.
5. test_differentiated_source_waters_produce_different_ph: After equilibrating (100 hours), tank with soft_acidic source → lower pH than tank with hard_shrimp source. Assert pH difference > 0.5.
6. test_ro_water_minimal_buffering: RO-like source water has very low KH/alkalinity. Water change with RO water reduces buffering capacity. Assert alkalinity decreases proportionally.
7. test_source_water_validation: Source water profiles with negative or NaN DIC/alkalinity → rejected with clear error.

Integration test:
8. test_source_water_ph_story: Run nano_cycle scenario twice: once with soft_acidic source, once with hard_shrimp source. After 500 hours, soft water tank should have lower pH and show faster pH decline from nitrification (less buffering). Hard water tank should maintain more stable pH. Assert with envelope bounds.
